## Automated Tests Required

### villager-ai-005 — Deciding scheduler (FIFO + `max_deciding_per_tick` budget) — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/villager_ai/deciding_scheduler_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- N > `max_deciding_per_tick` villagers become eligible in one tick → exactly the budgeted count run
  a Deciding pass that tick; the rest stay queued in stable (villager-index) order and drain FIFO on
  subsequent ticks.
- A villager mid-Deciding-pass is never interrupted by the next tick's budget check (budget caps
  passes STARTED, not duration).
- AC36: under a `max_ticks_per_frame` burst, at most one decision re-evaluation per processed tick,
  in order.
- Deciding completes within the tick with no visible "stand and think" pause (state assigned before
  the next tick).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Budget = 1 (spike default single-villager-per-tick case).
- Empty queue (no-op, no error).
- Enqueue order preserved across multiple ticks with a partially-drained queue.

**Estimated test count**: ~6-7

---

### villager-ai-006 — Activity priority decision loop (need > work > wander) — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/villager_ai/priority_decision_loop_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- AC1/AC2/AC3: strict discrete priority ordering across the three tiers, with the urgent-need
  boundary mocked per the story's own Engine Notes (Needs & Mood is not yet built — do not wait for
  it).
- AC4: Working + need becomes urgent → `decision_interval` re-check completes the current tick's
  work, releases the claim, pursues the need (graceful preemption, not an abrupt interrupt).
- AC41: Working + no urgent need → the periodic re-check produces no state change and no job
  re-selection — claims are sticky; this is the negative-case companion to AC4 and equally
  important (a naive implementation could re-run job selection every re-check and silently violate
  claim stickiness).
- AC5: the tick counter does not increment between activity-end and state assignment within one
  `decide()` call.
- Edge Case 3b: an urgent-need signal firing while already Traveling toward that same need is a
  no-op (not a redundant re-decide).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Preemption fires exactly at a cell-completion boundary vs. mid-cell (does "complete the current
  tick's work" mean the in-progress cell, not the in-progress command?).
- No jobs and no urgent needs → wanders indefinitely with no error (delegates target to Story 019,
  but the "no crash on empty everything" case belongs here).

**Estimated test count**: ~7-8

### villager-ai-007 — AStar3D graph build & shortest-path query — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/villager_ai/astar_graph_test.gd`

**What to test** (HIGH engine-risk story — cross-reference every AStar3D call against
`docs/engine-reference/godot/` before assuming a 4.3-era signature):
- Graph build: a point exists for every `is_standable` cell in a synthetic region; connections exist
  for every `is_step_legal` pair and for no illegal pair.
- **Deterministic bit-packed IDs — the nav-race precondition**: `_cell_to_astar_id(cell)` returns the
  identical ID for the same cell on repeated calls, and distinct IDs for distinct cells across the
  region bound — assert directly against the bit-pack formula (`x&0x1FFFFF | y<<21 | z<<42`), not
  just "IDs look different." This is the load-bearing fact ADR-0007 names: `AStar3D` never
  auto-recycles IDs on `remove_point()`, so an incrementing-counter scheme would drift under the
  add/remove churn villager-ai-008 introduces next. **This test is the direct evidence the
  nav-race assertions (see Smoke Test Scope) depend on.**
- Path cost: `path_length_cells` reflects ~1.0 orthogonal / ~1.4 diagonal weighting (F1); a target on
  the current/adjacent cell yields length 0 (immediate arrival).
- The graph never exceeds the `nav_region_size` settlement-core bound (assert point count is bounded,
  never full-world).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Unreachable target returns an empty path (no exception, no infinite search).
- A cell at the exact region-bound edge.

**Estimated test count**: ~6-7

---

### villager-ai-008 — Incremental AStar3D patching on cell writes — Integration
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/integration/villager_ai/graph_patching_test.gd`

**What to test** (HIGH engine-risk — this story + 009 together close the nav-race the sprint brief
names explicitly):
- Incremental patch, never a rebuild: a `cell_changed` that turns a standable cell solid updates only
  that cell's neighborhood points/connections — assert other points are untouched (no full rebuild;
  could be asserted via a call-count/point-identity check, not just "still passes").
- Dig-order/demolition writes (which also change standability) patch the graph identically to build
  writes.
- **AC49, the negative filter — the sprint's named perf/correctness assertion**: a write that does
  NOT intersect a moving villager's remaining movement cells or clearance envelope triggers **zero**
  re-path evaluations for that villager — assert call-count == 0, not just "no crash."
- **AC18, the positive filter**: a write that DOES intersect the remaining path triggers a re-path
  evaluation.
- **ID idempotency — the other nav-race precondition**: re-adding a previously-removed cell reuses
  its deterministic bit-pack ID (never a fresh/incremented one) — this is what makes repeated
  add/remove churn safe across many ticks.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- The clearance envelope's exact shape (each movement cell + two cells above + flanking orthogonals
  for diagonal steps) — test a write that is adjacent-but-outside the envelope (must NOT trigger)
  vs. one just inside it (must trigger).
- The filter applies uniformly across all "moving" cases named in the story (Traveling, a Wandering
  step, a Breather step-away, an F4 vacate step) — at minimum assert the Traveling case fully; note
  if the other three are deferred to villager-ai-009/019/021's own test files instead of duplicated
  here.

**Estimated test count**: ~6-7

---

### villager-ai-009 — Traveling state: path following + mid-travel re-path — Integration
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/integration/villager_ai/traveling_repath_test.gd`

**What to test** (HIGH engine-risk — this is the other half of the nav-race closure; per
ADR-0009 Decision, the race closure is: synchronous `cell_changed` emission lets the re-path filter
redirect a villager **before** its next frame's `_visual_position` interpolation step):
- Normal path following: `current_cell` advances cell-by-cell along the AStar3D path; arrival
  transitions to the next state (Working/Sleeping/etc.).
- **AC18 — mid-travel re-path**: a blocking write mid-travel → the villager re-paths from its current
  cell (drives villager-ai-008's positive filter through a real graph patch, not a mock).
- **AC19 — dead-target exit**: the travel target becomes invalid before arrival (bed destroyed, job
  voided) with no re-path possible → the villager exits to Deciding and re-selects; never keeps
  traveling toward a dead target. Assert the per-target fallback: job → report + release claim;
  bed → fall back to ground sleep; wander → pick a new target.
- **The race-closure assertion itself — name this test explicitly, do not fold it into AC18**: a
  Voxel World write at the villager's `to_cell` fires mid-transit → assert the redirect happens
  within the **same synchronous call stack** as the write's `cell_changed` emission (not deferred to
  next frame) — before `_visual_position` advances any further toward the now-solid cell. This is
  ADR-0009's own load-bearing test recommendation (Decision §3, Testing Considerations) and is the
  single most important assertion in this sprint's nav-race closure.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A re-path signal arriving when the villager has zero remaining path (already at target this tick)
  — no-op, not an error.
- Verify no code path reads `_visual_position` for any logic decision (grep companion, per the
  story's own Forbidden clause).

**Estimated test count**: ~6-7

### building-029 — Construction tick loop (Planned→UnderConstruction→Built) — Logic
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/unit/building_system/construction_tick_loop_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- AC20: a Planned cell fed `base_build_ticks` via a mocked on-site job → the Voxel World write occurs
  and the cell is Built on the last tick (F3, unit-testable without Villager AI — mock the job claim).
- AC22/AC26: zero tick events → UnderConstruction progress unchanged; paused halts construction while
  commits still work normally.
- AC24 (warp invariance): warp 2x → wall-clock halves, tick count to complete unchanged.
- AC25/AC45 (burst rule, per-villager): a burst of 10 ticks with the current cell needing 2 more →
  that cell completes and no further queued cell receives leftover ticks that frame; with two
  villagers on distinct cells, each completes independently and at most one cell per villager per
  frame — excess ticks never roll over.
- AC43: a mocked job-claim on a Planned cell → the cell transitions to UnderConstruction, queryable
  as distinct from Planned.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Fewer ticks than `base_build_ticks` leaves the cell UnderConstruction (not Built).
- Two villagers claiming distinct cells of the same command in the same burst (AC45's own scenario).

**Estimated test count**: ~8-9

### scene-004 — GameWorld scene assembly + headless E2E LOOP test — THE CROWN — Integration
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/integration/scene_world/gameworld_e2e_loop_test.gd`

**What to test** (HIGH risk — the historical failure mode named in the story and the sprint's own
Risk register is that integration/wiring gaps surface only at assembly; keep the four ACs as four
independently-diagnosable assertion groups in the same test scene, per the story's own Guardrail):
- **AC-ASSEMBLY**: a headless boot wires Voxel World (grid + mesher), Camera & Input, Building
  System, and Villager AI into GameWorld via `injected_tier_modules` (DI, ADR-0001) and boots through
  the ADR-0005 initialization gate — assert all four modules present, wired, and Ready; assert no
  module holds a non-DI cross-reference (grep companion).
- **AC-PLACE-A-BLOCK**: an armed tool + valid pick, committed through the real pick pipeline
  (ray → DDA → building-021 commit → building-029 construction ticks) → the target cell is Built in
  Voxel World grid data AND **exactly one** `cells_changed_batch` fires for the completion frame
  (consumes vox-003's DONE exactly-one-signal guarantee) — assert both halves of this condition, not
  just "the write happened."
- **AC-VILLAGER-WALKS**: a villager runs a Deciding pass (005/006), queries an AStar3D path (007),
  and follows it cell-by-cell (008/009) to arrival — assert on discrete `current_cell` transitions
  ending at the target, never on `_visual_position` or wall-clock timing.
- **AC-E2E-GATE**: the test is present in the commit gate and includes the **typed-Array crash-class
  regression call** — this is the recurring bug class named in the sprint's own Risk register (0
  incidents across S1-S5, "low but watched" — this is exactly the kind of regression an assembled
  scene first exercises at scale, so keep the explicit call, do not let it quietly drop out during
  implementation).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A half-failure is diagnosable in isolation: if AC-PLACE-A-BLOCK fails, AC-VILLAGER-WALKS's
  assertions should still run and report independently (structure the test so one `assert_*` failure
  does not abort the whole suite before the other half runs, or split into two test functions in the
  same file if the framework's failure semantics require it).
- Both halves consume in-sprint stories (021+029, and 009 which itself chains through 005-008) — if
  any upstream Must story slips, this test cannot be written meaningfully yet. Do not stub around a
  missing dependency to make the crown "pass green" prematurely — an artificially-passing E2E test
  is worse than an honestly-red one for this story specifically, since it is the milestone's
  criterion-#8 signal.

**Estimated test count**: ~4 assertion groups, likely 8-10 individual test functions once each group's
edge cases are split out (the two halves plus assembly plus the regression call, each with at least
one boundary case).

### vox-014 — Load-before-write for far-world (non-resident) mutations (Should) — Integration
**Test file path**: `neues-spiel/tests/integration/voxel_world/load_before_write_test.gd`
(or a documented playtest — see Classification Note #4)

**What to test** (HIGH risk — a dropped or blind far-world write is data loss):
- AC-1: a write to a cell in a non-resident chunk → the chunk's region pages in, the resident copy is
  written, marked dirty, and eventual staggered eviction flushes it — the region file is never
  written blind.
- AC-2: a far-world write arriving while its page-in is still in flight is deferred until the
  resident copy exists, then applied — never dropped, never written straight to disk.
- **AC-3, the single-location rule**: the dig-order path (Story 009, Voxel World epic) inherits
  load-before-write with **no dig-order-specific residency code** — assert (or grep) that the rule
  lives only in the single batched write path, not duplicated per caller.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Two far writes to the same non-resident chunk coalesce onto one page-in (not two redundant
  dispatches).

**Estimated test count**: ~5-6

## Manual QA Checklist

### Windowed play-check over the assembled GameWorld (ADVISORY) — first meaningful pass, scene-004
**Why this exists, and why now**: every prior sprint's windowed check (Sprint 2's D3D12 backend
init, Sprint 3's orbit-only feel check, Sprint 4's zoom/pan-over-rendered-terrain check) ran against
a scene that was rendering geometry but had no playable loop behind it yet — there was nothing to
*do*, only something to look at. Sprint 6's crown is the first sprint where an assembled, playable
build exists: a real pick→commit→construction-tick block placement and a real decide→path→walk
villager, both live in one running scene. This is the first time a windowed play-check answers a
question no headless test can: does the assembled loop *feel* coherent to a human watching it,
end-to-end, in real time?

**Sprint 4's camera-feel-check advisory folds into this pass rather than remaining separate.**
Sprint 4 left "orbit/zoom/pan feel correct over rendered terrain" as its own open advisory item
(`qa-plan-sprint-4-2026-07-24.md`); no evidence doc for it exists yet in `production/qa/evidence/`
(only a `camera-sandbox-check.png` screenshot, no written sign-off) — it appears to have been
carried forward rather than closed. Re-running it standalone against Sprint 6's assembled scene
would just be the same check against a richer background; folding it into the loop pass avoids a
duplicate windowed session. **This is a scope proposal, not a decision — user's judgment is still
pending on whether to fold it in this way or keep it as a separate open item.**

**Verification method**: Manual step-through (windowed, non-`--headless` launch)
**Who must sign off**: qa-lead (or game-designer if a feel/subjective call is disputed)
**Evidence to capture**: one screenshot of the placed block + one of the villager mid-walk, plus a
short written note in `production/qa/evidence/`

Checklist:
- [ ] Placing a block via the real tool (armed tool, pick, click/drag, commit) shows the ghost →
      commit → under-construction → built visual progression without a jarring pop or a frame where
      the geometry looks wrong
- [ ] A villager visibly walks cell-by-cell toward a target with no visual teleport/snap and no
      clipping through geometry (this is the human-observable companion to the headless
      `current_cell`-only assertions — a race-closure regression would likely show here as a visible
      clip before it shows in a log)
- [ ] Orbit (mmb-drag + Q/E), zoom (wheel), and pan (WASD) still feel correct over the now-populated
      scene — carried forward from Sprint 4, now exercised against real building + villager content
      instead of empty/terrain-only geometry
- [ ] Toggling pause or time-warp (1x/2x/3x) mid-construction and mid-walk produces the expected
      effect (construction/travel pace changes accordingly; camera feel itself is unaffected per the
      raw-delta contract) — this is a qualitative companion to building-029's AC24 and villager-ai
      warp-invariance tests, not a substitute for them

*ADVISORY — per `/qa-plan` protocol this does not block scene-004 (or any story) out of Done on its
own; the BLOCKING evidence is the headless E2E LOOP test above. This is the natural companion check
now that there is, for the first time, a playable loop worth watching.*

## Smoke Test Scope

**Baseline**: 524 passing tests (per `sprint-06.md`'s own Sprint 5 actuals: "Test suite green at 524
headless (GdUnit4), zero red" at Sprint 5's close).

**What Sprint 6 adds**: up to 13 new test files (8 committed Must + 4 Should + 1 Nice), summing to
roughly **~55-60 tests from the 8 committed Must stories** (villager-ai-005 ~6-7, 006 ~7-8, 007 ~6-7,
008 ~6-7, 009 ~6-7, building-021 ~5-6, building-029 ~8-9, scene-004 ~8-10) plus **~19-22 more if all
4 Should stories land** (building-022 ~6-7, vox-013 ~4-5, vox-014 ~5-6, tick-006 ~3-4) plus **~4-5
more if the Nice item lands** (vox-015 ~4-5). Target regression count at sprint close: **~579-584**
(committed-only) or **~598-606** (if all four Should land) or **~602-611** (if the Nice item also
lands) — zero failures, zero errors, zero skipped.

1. **Full regression suite runs green**: all 524 existing tests PLUS every new Sprint-6 test file
   above via `tests\run-tests.cmd` — 524 is a floor, not a ceiling.

2. **THE E2E LOOP TEST (scene-004) is smoke item #1 — the new canonical smoke gate, the way
   spine-004 was the canonical smoke item for boot.** Nothing else in this list matters if this
   fails, because the crown is the milestone's criterion-#8 signal:
   - `neues-spiel/tests/integration/scene_world/gameworld_e2e_loop_test.gd` runs headless and green,
     asserting BOTH halves independently (AC-PLACE-A-BLOCK and AC-VILLAGER-WALKS) — a half-failure
     must be visible as a distinct red, not folded into one pass/fail line.
   - The typed-Array crash-class regression call (AC-E2E-GATE) fires and passes — this is the
     recurring bug class the sprint's own Risk register is watching (0 incidents S1-S5); a smoke
     pass here re-confirms it, it does not assume it from story-completion time.
   - This test is re-run at smoke/hand-off time even if it passed at scene-004's own
     story-completion — the same discipline Sprint 5 applied to the residency-invariant items,
     because assembly-time wiring is exactly where a later Sprint-6 story touching a shared file
     (e.g., building-022 or vox-013/014 landing after scene-004) could silently break the wiring.

3. **Nav-race assertions — named explicitly per ADR-0007/ADR-0009, not folded into a generic
   villager-AI line (the sprint brief's own risk concentration for the ai-programmer lane):**
   - **AStar3D IDs never auto-recycled** (ADR-0007): grep/re-confirm the deterministic bit-pack ID
     scheme (`_cell_to_astar_id`) is the only ID source — zero incrementing-counter variables
     (e.g., a `_next_id`-style field) anywhere in the villager AI nav code. Re-confirm the
     idempotency case from villager-ai-008's own test (re-adding a removed cell reuses its ID) still
     holds after villager-ai-009 lands and starts exercising add/remove churn during real travel.
   - **Synchronous `cell_changed` patching is load-bearing for the race closure** (ADR-0009): the
     race-closure test named in villager-ai-009 (a write at `to_cell` mid-transit redirects within
     the same synchronous call stack, before `_visual_position` advances) is re-run at smoke time,
     not assumed still-true. Grep confirms the `cell_changed` connection between Voxel World and
     Villager AI is NOT `CONNECT_DEFERRED` (a deferred connection would silently reopen the race
     ADR-0009 closed).
   - **Zero `NavigationServer3D`/`NavigationAgent3D`/`NavigationRegion3D`** in Villager AI or Build
     Validation (`rg --glob "*.gd" "NavigationServer3D|NavigationAgent3D|NavigationRegion3D"
     src/villager_ai/`) — zero matches, extending the Sprint 4/5 guardrail through the graph-build
     and patching stories.
   - **Zero `Thread`/`WorkerThreadPool` in Villager AI** (`rg --glob "*.gd"
     "Thread|WorkerThreadPool" src/villager_ai/`) — zero matches (the residency tier's
     `WorkerThreadPool` usage lives in Voxel World, not here — confirm the boundary is not crossed
     now that villager-ai-008 patches on `cell_changed` from that same residency tier).

4. **The two newly-certifiable ADR-0015 invariants — named explicitly, conditional on vox-013/014
   landing (Should, not Must):**
   - **Read-through in-flight-write cache (vox-013)**: a re-needed evicting-dirty chunk is served
     from `_write_in_flight_data`, never a torn region read — re-run vox-013's own AC-1/AC-2
     assertions at smoke time. **If vox-013 does not land this sprint, this item is N/A — do not
     read a green smoke pass as certifying it; state so explicitly at hand-off**, per the same
     discipline Sprint 5 used when 013/014 were out of scope.
   - **Load-before-write for far-world mutations (vox-014)**: a non-resident write pages in →
     resident-copy write → mark dirty → staggered flush, with the rule living in exactly ONE place
     (the single batched write path) — re-run vox-014's AC-1/AC-2/AC-3 at smoke time. Same N/A
     caveat if vox-014 is cut.
   - **If both land**: this is the point at which the full ADR-0015 invariant set named across
     Stories 010-014 is closed (010/011/012 certified at Sprint 5's close; 013/014 close here) —
     worth stating explicitly in the sign-off report as a milestone-relevant fact, not just a
     per-story checkbox.

5. **Building System grep-guard families — extends the Sprint 5 precedent to this sprint's new
   commit/tick-loop/validity stories:**
   - Zero physics API calls in the pick/commit path: `rg --glob "*.gd"
     "intersect_ray|PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D|RayCast3D" src/building_system/` — zero matches.
   - Zero `PhysicsServer3D`/`RayCast3D` anywhere in Building System.
   - Blueprint cells remain invisible to Voxel World's raw data layer until building-029's
     tick-completion write — grep/assert no premature `set_cell` call exists in the commit path
     (building-021's own explicit non-goal until 029's write).

6. **Project-wide forbidden patterns — now covering scene-004's assembly code and tick-006's own
   guard**: `rg --glob "*.gd" "SceneTree\.paused|Engine\.time_scale"` across `neues-spiel/` — zero
   matches. This is the first sprint where the assembly scene itself (scene-004) is new surface
   area for this check, and tick-006 adds its own dedicated regression grep on top.

7. **CW-winding / culling regression (carried forward, unaffected by this sprint's stories)**:
   `CULL_DISABLED` grep for committed-block terrain material — zero matches, per the Sprint 4 gate,
   now exercised for the first time against a scene that also renders placed/under-construction
   blocks (building-029's write path), not just generated terrain.

8. **Engine-risk cross-reference (HIGH-risk stories this sprint)**: `AStar3D`'s API surface
   (`add_point`, `connect_points`, `disconnect_points`, `remove_point`, `has_point`, `get_id_path`,
   `get_point_path`) as used by villager-ai-007/008/009, and `WorkerThreadPool`/`FileAccess` shapes
   as used by vox-013/014, are confirmed against `docs/engine-reference/godot/` before trusting any
   test that assumes their behavior — all five stories are flagged HIGH risk in their own headers.

9. **Performance is within budget** — this is the first sprint where Building + Villager AI + the
   mesher + camera all run in one assembled scene simultaneously (previous sprints tested each tier
   in isolation):
   - No frame-time regression from running the construction-tick loop and the Deciding-scheduler
     budget (`max_deciding_per_tick`) concurrently — spot-check via the E2E test's own timing, or a
     code-review note if no in-engine profile exists yet.
   - vox-015 (Nice, if landed) makes the 60-FPS-with-culling measurement possible for the first
     time on the production view window — if it lands, re-confirm draw calls stay ≤ 2000 with the
     assembled scene's added building/villager geometry, not just bare terrain.
   - If vox-015 does NOT land, state explicitly that the 60-FPS-with-culling measurement remains
     unmeasurable this sprint (same "flag rather than silently skip" discipline Sprint 5 applied to
     its own unmeasured-performance note) — do not let this look like an oversight.

*Smoke tests are verified by the developer via `/smoke-check sprint`. Reference this list when

## Playtest Requirements

| Story | Playtest Goal | Min Sessions | Target Player Type |
|-------|--------------|--------------|-------------------|
| scene-004 (companion, not primary evidence) | Does the assembled build-and-inhabit loop read as coherent to a human watching it end-to-end? | 1 (the windowed play-check above) | qa-lead / game-designer (engineering feel-check, not a broad playtester pool yet) |

**No mandatory external playtest sessions required for this sprint.** Every committed Logic/
Integration story's primary evidence path is an automated headless test; the windowed play-check
above is an engineering/feel spot-check (Manual QA Checklist), not a player-feedback session with a
questionnaire — same posture Sprint 4 used for its camera-feel check.

- **vox-013, vox-014, and vox-015** each declare "integration test OR documented playtest" as their
  own alternate evidence path (Sprint 5 precedent for vox-010/011/012). If any team elects the
  playtest route, it must be written to `production/session-logs/playtest-sprint-6-[story-slug].md`,
  reviewed by qa-lead, and — per Classification Note #4 — must name the specific correctness
  condition it verified (not a generic "seemed fine" note), since vox-013/014 are HIGH-risk
  correctness mechanisms.
- The first genuinely broader playtest (a real player pool reacting to the build-and-inhabit loop,
  not just an engineering feel-check) becomes warranted once the fully-closed job loop
  (building-030 + villager-ai-011/012, Sprint 7 per this sprint's own Out-of-Scope note) lets a
  villager actually complete a player-placed block end-to-end. This sprint's crown proves the two
  halves coexist in one scene; Sprint 7 closes them into one loop a player would recognize as
  "I built something and someone built it." Re-evaluate playtest scope then.

## Definition of Done — This Sprint

A story is DONE when ALL of the following are true:

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified — via a passing automated test result. By declared Type:
      **6 Logic** stories (villager-ai-005/006/007, building-021/029, +Should building-022);
      **7 Integration** stories (villager-ai-008/009, scene-004, +Should vox-013/014/tick-006,
      +Nice vox-015 if pulled) — OR documented manual evidence for the declared alternate-path
      stories (vox-013/014/015's playtest alternate, if elected, meeting the bar in Classification
      Note #4)
- [ ] Test file exists at the canonical path listed in this plan's Test Summary table for all
      in-scope stories that land
- [ ] **The E2E LOOP test (scene-004) passes headless, asserting BOTH halves independently
      (place-a-block AND villager-walks), includes the typed-Array regression call, and is wired
      into the commit gate** — this is the sprint's own hard exit condition (Milestone 01
      criterion #8 begins here) and is not satisfiable by any manual evidence substitute
- [ ] tick-006 (Should) has its own passing integration test — flagged in Classification Note #1 as
      omitted from the sprint file's own DoD prose; this plan requires it regardless
- [ ] All AStar3D / nav / threading APIs (villager-ai-007/008/009) confirmed against
      `docs/engine-reference/godot/` before any test trusts their behavior
- [ ] The windowed play-check (Manual QA Checklist) is either completed and signed off, or
      explicitly declined by the user — not silently skipped; if completed, folds in Sprint 4's
      still-open camera-feel item per this plan's proposal (pending user confirmation)
- [ ] Full regression suite passes (`/smoke-check sprint`) — 524-test baseline plus every new
      Sprint-6 test file, zero failures/errors/skips, **plus the E2E LOOP test (smoke item #1), the
      nav-race assertions (item 3), and the two ADR-0015 invariants if vox-013/014 land (item 4)
      explicitly re-checked at hand-off, not assumed still-true from story-completion time**
- [ ] If vox-013 and/or vox-014 do not land this sprint, the smoke report states explicitly which
      ADR-0015 invariants remain uncertified — no green smoke pass is read as certifying a story
      that was not committed
- [ ] No regressions introduced — carried-forward project-wide forbidden patterns
      (`SceneTree.paused`, `Engine.time_scale`, zero-physics picking, `CULL_DISABLED`,
      `NavigationServer3D`-family, `Thread`/`WorkerThreadPool` in Villager AI) remain absent,
      re-checked against this sprint's new assembly surface (scene-004) and new villager-nav files
      (007/008/009)
- [ ] No open S1 or S2 bugs in delivered stories
- [ ] Code reviewed (via `/code-review` or documented peer review)
- [ ] Story file updated to `Status: Complete` (via `/story-done`)

This plan corrects `sprint-06.md`'s own Definition of Done in one place (Classification Note #1):
tick-006 requires the same BLOCKING automated-test evidence as vox-013/014, even though the sprint
file's DoD prose lists only the latter two by name. All 13 in-scope stories carry BLOCKING
automated-test evidence if they land (matching Sprint 5's 8-of-8 ratio, extended to a larger story
set) — because this sprint, like Sprint 5, has no primary Visual/Feel or UI story. The one manual
item this plan calls for (the windowed play-check) is ADVISORY and does not gate any story's Done
status; it exists because, for the first time this milestone, there is an assembled playable loop
worth a human watching end-to-end.
